Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes.md)

# Flow Nodes

Every node the [Flow editor](https://docs.theprototype.app/node-system.md) offers, grouped exactly as the palette groups
them. Each node's one-line description is the same text the editor shows in its info pane
(and the palette's tooltip) when you select the node, so the two cannot disagree. Nodes with
their own page link to it.

Since 1.23 every node's properties are in the node editor's **ⓘ Params** tab, and a double-click on a
node with code (Script, Behaviour, a module's node) opens that code — see
[Main graph & node properties](https://docs.theprototype.app/main-graph.md).

## Input

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Slider**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md) | An interactive slider that outputs a number - the quickest way to hand-tune any numeric input live. |
| [**Color Picker**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/colorpicker.md) | Outputs a color chosen with a swatch - the color source for anything that paints. |
| [**Switcher**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/switcher.md) | A radio-button list that outputs the index of the selected item. Each item also has an input: the value output passes on whatever is wired into the selected item (a multi-way switch). Wire a number into index to choose by graph instead of by hand. |
| [**Number**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/number.md) | A constant numeric value - the simplest source node. |
| [**Vector3**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/vector3.md) | An x/y/z triple - used as a direction, an offset, or most often a fixed point in the world. |
| [**Toggle**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/toggle.md) | A checkbox that outputs true or false - a hand-operated on/off switch. |
| [**Random**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/random.md) | A random number in a range - deterministic, so every peer sees the same "random" value. |
| [**Time**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time.md) | The synced clock as a value - the heartbeat behind almost every animation recipe. |

## Scene

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Object Selector**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md) | Binds the graph to a scene object - the sink every effect must reach, and an object reference for sensor nodes. |
| [**Velocity**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity.md) | Outputs how fast the connected object is moving right now, in metres per second. |
| [**Measure**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/measure.md) | Reads a number off an object: how tall it is, where its top is, how fast it is going. |
| [**Spawn**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spawn.md) | Makes copies of an object while the simulation runs - crates off a conveyor, targets, debris, ammo, waves of anything. |

## Object Flow

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Flow Input**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowinput.md) | Declares a public input socket for an object flow - the way the Scene flow feeds a value into an object's own graph. |
| [**Flow Output**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput.md) | Declares a public output socket for an object flow - the way an object publishes a value back to the Scene flow. |
| [**Object Flow**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md) | Embeds an object's own graph into the Scene flow as a single card - the way to compose object flows into a bigger machine without opening each one. |

## Game

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Set Game State**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate.md) | Switches the shared game state (menu, playing, paused, over) when a pulse arrives - every peer follows the same state. |
| [**On Game State**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate.md) | Fires a pulse when the shared game state becomes the one you pick - the hook for "when the round starts". |
| [**Set Active Camera**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera.md) | Makes a camera object the active view for every player when a pulse arrives. |
| [**Camera Rig**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/camerarig.md) | Moves a camera object: it follows the target at an offset and/or turns to look at it, with damping (seconds of lag). Wire it into an Object Selector that picks a camera. It never moves the editor view or another player's view - look through the camera (Set Active Camera) to see it. |
| [**Set Look**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setlook.md) | Switches a camera's look (its post-processing) on or off when a pulse arrives, and by default looks through that camera too. |
| [**Game Start**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamestart.md) | Fires once when the game starts (Play, or a round reset) - the place to spawn, reset counters and arm timers. |
| [**Travel to scene**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/travel.md) | Loads another saved scene by name when a pulse arrives - a door to the next level, replicated to everyone. |
| [**All Players**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/allplayers.md) | Iterates the connected players so a per-player value can be read, or a HUD row shown, for each of them. |
| [**Set Variable**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable.md) | Stores a named value in the replicated scene variables when a pulse arrives - shared state without an object. |
| [**Get Variable**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md) | Reads a named scene variable as a value - the read side of Set Variable, live on every peer. |
| [**Store Value**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md) | Saves a value on THIS device when a pulse arrives (set, keep the max or min, or add) - a best score or a level reached that survives a reload; never sent to other players. |
| [**Stored Value**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue.md) | Reads what Store Value saved on this device, as a number or text - the read side of a best score; each player sees their own. |
| [**Announce**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/announce.md) | Shows a big banner - 'Ring 2 reached', 'GOAL!' - on every screen and in VR when a pulse arrives; {v} in the text shows a wired number. |
| [**Game Sound**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamesound.md) | Plays one of the built-in game sounds (coin, ring, levelup, cheer...) when a pulse arrives, at the wired object if one is wired; no sound files needed. |
| [**Effect Burst**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/effectburst.md) | Fires a short sparkle, confetti, smoke or sparks burst at the wired object (or in front of the player) when a pulse arrives; pooled and local to each device. |
| [**Controller Buzz**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hapticpulse.md) | Buzzes the VR controllers with a named pattern (tap, bump, success...) when a pulse arrives - only in Interact or Play, never while editing. |
| [**Game Music**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamemusic.md) | Plays a looping built-in music preset while you are in Interact or Play - always, or only during a round; wire 'on' to switch it by a condition. |
| [**Game Setting**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamesetting.md) | Declares one row in the game's Settings (a toggle, a range or a choice) and outputs this player's value - saved on this device for this game, never shared. |
| [**Point Grab**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pointgrab.md) | While 'enabled' reads off, players cannot pick objects up by pointing at them (the VR grip ray, the desktop carry); a hand touching an object still moves it. |
| [**On Clap**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclap.md) | Fires a pulse when a VR player brings both hands together and holds them - with where they met (point) and whether it was you (byMe); wire 'enabled' to a setting to switch it. |
| [**Game Time**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gametime.md) | Seconds since the game (or the round) started, the same on every peer - a clock that pauses with the game. |
| [**Player Variable**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/peervariable.md) | A value kept PER PLAYER (score, lives, team) - each peer reads its own row, or a named player's. |

## Logic

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Script**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/script.md) | Your own JavaScript - an effect that moves its object every frame, or (with declared typed inputs and outputs) a small pure function whose return feeds other nodes. v2 scripts also get `api`: object(uuid or name), raycast(from, dir), and in effects keys() (this device only) and spawn('/create ...') (the host spawns once for everyone). |
| [**Behaviour**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/behaviour.md) | Game logic written as a small JavaScript file (params, replicated state, event handlers, kit calls) - run once on the authority peer, with a live node view of its events, state and knobs. |
| [**Code link**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/coderef.md) | Points at the module or kit file whose code runs part of this game - double-click (or Open code) to read it. It does nothing at runtime; it is how the Main graph shows where every rule lives. |
| [**Math**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/math.md) | Combines numbers (+ - * / min max mod pow) or shapes one: sin/cos (b scales them, 0 = 1), abs, round, floor, clamp to 0..b, negate. + input adds sockets (up to 8) for + - * / min max. |
| [**Compare**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md) | Compares two numbers and outputs true or false. |
| [**Gate**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gate.md) | Boolean logic - AND, OR, NOT, XOR. + input adds sockets (up to 8): AND = all true, OR = any true, XOR = an odd number true. |
| [**Map Range**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/maprange.md) | Remaps a number from one range to another - the glue between free-range sources and bounded parameters. |
| [**Select**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/select.md) | Picks one of up to four values (a, b, c, d) by a rounded index. |
| [**Latch**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/latch.md) | Holds a boolean until told otherwise - set, reset and toggle pulses make it a memory bit. |
| [**Delay**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/delay.md) | Passes a pulse on after a set number of seconds - the timing of a fuse, or a door that closes later. |
| [**Sequence**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/sequence.md) | Fires its outputs one after another, one per pulse, then wraps around - a step-by-step trigger. |
| [**Once**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/once.md) | Lets exactly one pulse through until it is re-armed - a checkpoint, a pickup, a first-time event. |
| [**Counter**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md) | Counts trigger pulses and outputs the running total. |
| [**Loop**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/loop.md) | Sweeps a number from one value to another over time, repeating - a ready-made animation ramp. |
| [**Timer**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/timer.md) | A delay line: outputs its input as it was a set number of seconds ago. |
| [**Distance**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/distance.md) | Measures the live distance between two things in the scene. |
| [**Proximity**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/proximity.md) | True while two things are within a radius of each other - a distance sensor with the threshold built in. |
| [**Look At**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/lookat.md) | Keeps the connected object facing a target - another object or a fixed point - every frame. |
| [**Set Color**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcolor.md) | Paints the connected object's material with a color, re-applied every frame. |
| [**Visibility**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/visibility.md) | Shows or hides the connected object based on a boolean. |
| [**Set Shader Uniform**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setuniform.md) | Writes one number inside an object's shader graph, so a trigger, a |

## Triggers

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**On Click**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md) | Fires a short pulse when its object is clicked - the bridge from user input into the graph. |
| [**On Grab**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongrab.md) | Fires a pulse when a player picks the object up - a carry in Play or Interact, or a VR grip in Interact; editor moves never fire it. |
| [**Key Press**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/keypress.md) | Fires a pulse while a keyboard key is pressed - the bridge from your keyboard into the graph. |
| [**On Hit**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onhit.md) | Fires a pulse when a hand or a walking player knocks the object - with how hard it was hit (speed) and whether you did it (byMe). |
| [**On Rest**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onrest.md) | Fires a pulse when a physics body has finished moving - the counterpart to On Impact, which fires when it starts. |
| [**Gamepad Button**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamepadbutton.md) | Fires a pulse (or holds a level) while a gamepad button is pressed - the pad's counterpart of Key Press. |
| [**Gamepad Axis**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamepadaxis.md) | A gamepad stick or trigger axis as a number between -1 and 1, with a dead zone. |

## Animation

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Shake**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/shake.md) | Jitters the connected object around its resting position - rumble, nervousness, impact feedback. |
| [**Spin**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spin.md) | Rotates the connected object continuously around one axis. |
| [**Rotate / Motor**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/rotor.md) | Turns the connected object about its own local axis (and its origin, so a wheel turns on its hub) at a set rpm with a spin-up. Paddles and scoops it turns carry water from Fluid emitters. On a dynamic physics body during a simulation it becomes a real motor: torque-limited, so a load slows it. |
| [**Float Along Flow**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowfloat.md) | Carries the connected object along a Flow path - a leaf, a toy boat - from where you placed it, at the path's speed, bobbing and turning with the current, looping at the end. Uses the nearest Flow path unless one is wired. |
| [**Bounce**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bounce.md) | Bounces the connected object up and down off its resting height, like a dribbled ball. |
| [**Orbit**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/orbit.md) | Circles the connected object around its resting position on the horizontal plane. |
| [**Path patrol**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pathpatrol.md) | Walks the connected object along a series of waypoints you click into the scene, facing along the path. |
| [**Follow Path**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/followpath.md) | Moves the connected object along a smooth path - a drawn Spline, a Flow path or its own waypoints - at a speed, looping, ping-ponging or once, facing along it and leaning into the turns. An offset spreads several riders out along one path. |
| [**Wander**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/wander.md) | Drifts the connected object around a smooth, never-repeating target inside an area object (a water volume, a room) or a box around where it was placed - fish, birds, fireflies, idle drones. |
| [**Orient to Velocity**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/orientvelocity.md) | Turns the connected object to face the way it is moving, smoothly, leaning into turns - put it after Wander, Orbit or any mover so it looks where it goes. |
| [**Body Wave**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bodywave.md) | Bends the connected object with a wave travelling along its body - a swimming fish, a snake, a flag, a tail - stronger and faster the faster it moves, curving into turns. A shader effect: physics and picking keep the rest pose. |
| [**Animation Finished**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animfinished.md) | Fires a pulse when the connected object's animation clip reaches its end. |
| [**Animation Marker**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animmarker.md) | Fires a pulse when the connected object's animation passes a named marker. |
| [**Animation State**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animstate.md) | Reads the connected object's animation transport as a number - playing, position or progress. |
| [**Play Animation**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/playanim.md) | Starts, stops or restarts an animation clip on the connected object when a pulse arrives. |
| [**Play Sequence**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/playseq.md) | Plays, stops, toggles or restarts a Timeline sequence (camera shots, clips, audio, events) for every player when a pulse arrives. |
| [**On Sequence Event**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onseqevent.md) | Fires a pulse when a running Timeline sequence passes a named event, or reaches its end ('end'). |

## Physics

On Impact, On Enter and On Exit sit here since 1.22. Each has an **only with** input (fire only for one other
object) and an **other** output (the body it touched) — see [Contact filters](https://docs.theprototype.app/colliders.md#contact-filters-only-with-and-other).

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**On Impact**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onimpact.md) | Fires a pulse when a physics simulation lands the connected object on the ground or another object. |
| [**On Enter**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onenter.md) | Fires a pulse when something enters a trigger volume - the checkpoint, doorway and pressure-plate node. |
| [**On Exit**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onexit.md) | Fires a pulse when something leaves a trigger volume - the other half of On Enter. |
| [**Mass**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/mass.md) | Gives the connected object weight for the physics simulation - objects with a Mass fall and collide. |
| [**Bounciness**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bounciness.md) | Sets how much the connected object rebounds in the physics simulation (restitution). |
| [**Friction**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/friction.md) | Sets how much the connected object grips surfaces in the physics simulation. |
| [**Angular Velocity**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/angularvelocity.md) | Gives the connected object a constant spin under physics - a rolling barrel, a spinning hazard, a rotating platform other objects can stand on. |
| [**Collider**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/collider.md) | Overrides the collision shape the physics simulation uses for the connected object - the flow equivalent of the Inspector's Physics > Collider pick, and it wins over it. |
| [**Motor**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/motor.md) | Drives every hinge joint attached to the connected object - the flow way to make wheels turn, turntables spin and doors swing under power. |
| [**Impulse**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/impulse.md) | Pushes or spins a physics body when an event fires - a jump, a kick, a cannon, a nudge. |
| [**Set Velocity**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvelocity.md) | Sets a physics body's speed outright - to launch it at an exact velocity, to hold it at a constant one, or to stop it dead. |
| [**Joint**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/joint.md) | Attaches two objects to each other when an event fires - a hinge, or a rigid weld. |

## Effects

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Pulse**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pulse.md) | Throbs the connected object's scale in and out around its resting size. |
| [**Blink**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/blink.md) | Flashes the connected object on and off at a steady rate. |
| [**Sound**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/sound.md) | Plays an Explorer audio clip on the connected object when a pulse arrives - spatial, replicated, by content hash. |
| [**Particles**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/particle.md) | Emits a particle effect from the connected object - a preset burst, a stream, a trail. |
| [**Jiggle**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/jiggle.md) | Makes the connected object jiggle - it lags behind when moved, wobbles like jelly on impact and sways in the wind; skinned models swing their bone chains. |

## Music

| Node | What it does |
|---|---|
| [**Device Param**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/deviceparam.md) | Writes a number into one parameter of the connected audio device every frame - an LFO on a cutoff, a fader on a level. |
| [**Device Level**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/devicelevel.md) | The live output level of the connected audio device (or a wired one) as a number - a meter you can drive anything with. |
| [**Transport**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/transportbeat.md) | The shared music transport as a number - beat, bar, phase, bpm or playing - identical on every peer. |
| [**Note Trigger**](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/notetrigger.md) | Plays a note on the connected audio device when a pulse arrives - a drum pad, a sampler pad, a synth key. |

## Kit

The [game kit](https://docs.theprototype.app/game-kit.md)'s nodes, one group per piece. Every node is generated from the same
description as the kit's code interface, and one peer applies each change, so a press seen by
every peer counts once. The [Game kit](https://docs.theprototype.app/game-kit.md#the-pieces) page lists them all.

| Group | What it covers |
|---|---|
| **Kit: Rules** | Grab reach, jump height and play bounds that every grab path obeys; a pulse when a grab is refused. |
| **Kit: Round** | Round setup, start, restart, pause, win, lose and add time; the phase, time left and countdown; an event for each step. |
| **Kit: Levels** | Go to a level, next level, finish a level, game mode; stars, unlocks and progress saved per device. |
| **Kit: Score** | Add, set and reset the score, counted once; my score, best score and the leader. |
| **Kit: Pickups** | Collect a pickup once for everybody, with respawn; how many are left; a "collect them all" event. |
| **Kit: Spawner** | Spawn entities as copies of a template, remove or clear them, count the living; an event when the wave is over. |
| **Kit: Health** | Damage, area damage, heal and revive entities; their hit points; damaged, healed, died and revived events. |
| **Kit: Mover** | Make entities chase a target round walls and each other, stop them, knock them back; an event when one is stuck. |

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows.md)

# Object Flows

Every object can now carry **its own node graph**, alongside the shared **Scene flow**. Object flows keep behavior with the thing it belongs to — a door knows how to open, a lamp knows how to flicker — and the Scene flow composes them.

## Scene flow vs object flows

- The **Scene flow** is the shared, world-level graph you have always had.
- An **object flow** is a private graph document owned by one object. All graphs replicate live to every peer and are saved with sessions, autosave and `.tpscene` exports.

The editor's scope **follows your selection**: select an object and the Flow editor shows *that object's* flow (the [breadcrumb bar](https://docs.theprototype.app/node-editor.md#the-breadcrumb-bar) at the top says which — tap its crumb to jump to another flow); deselect and you are back in the Scene flow. Flow Code shows whichever graph the editor is showing.

## Creating and deleting a flow

Select an object that has no flow yet — the editor shows **"<name> has no flow yet"** with a one-click **Create flow** button (adding a node from the palette creates it too). To remove one, open the object's flow and press the 🗑 at the right end of the breadcrumb bar; a **Delete this flow?** dialog says how many nodes will be removed for everyone. Deleting a flow is undoable — <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> restores the whole graph.

## No Object Selector needed

Inside an object flow, effect nodes (Spin, Bounce, Script, module nodes, Sound, physics params, On Click…) target **the owner object implicitly** — just drop a Spin node in a box's flow and the box spins. Wiring into an Object Selector still works and always wins, so an object's flow may also drive *other* objects.

## Public sockets: Flow Input / Flow Output

An object flow can declare an interface, like a function signature:

- **Flow Input** — a named, typed value source (number / boolean / vector3 / color). Inside the graph it outputs whatever the Scene feeds it (or its fallback).
- **Flow Output** — a named sink; whatever you wire into it becomes visible to the Scene. Its gray socket accepts **any value type**.

!!! warning "Outputs carry values, not effects"
    Animation/effect nodes (Spin, Pulse, Wobble… — the **orange** sockets) are not values and cannot wire into a Flow Output. Output the *driving value* instead: the Time, Slider, Math or Loop node that feeds the effect.

## Embedding a flow in the Scene graph

Once a flow declares inputs/outputs, embed it in the Scene flow as a single **Object Flow** node:

- right-click the object in the viewport → **Add flow to Scene graph**, or
- add an **Object Flow** node from the palette (Object Flow group) and pick the object — only objects that *have* flows are listed.

The embedded node shows the declared sockets: Scene values wired into it feed the flow's Flow Inputs; the flow's Flow Output values come out the other side (with one frame of latency). Renaming or deleting an interface node updates the embedded sockets everywhere and cleanly disconnects stale wires; deleting the flow removes its embedded node.

## Practical example

A breathing lamp whose intensity the Scene controls:

1. Select the lamp object → **Create flow**.
2. Add a **Flow Input** named `amount` (number) and a **Pulse** node; wire `amount → Pulse.amount`. The Pulse drives the lamp itself (no Object Selector needed).
3. Add a **Time** node (mode `sin`) and a **Flow Output** named `phase`; wire **Time → phase**. (The Time *value* is what leaves the flow — the Pulse effect itself stays inside.)
4. Deselect (back in the Scene flow), right-click the lamp → **Add flow to Scene graph**.
5. Wire a **Slider** into the embedded node's `amount` — the slider now breathes the lamp, and `phase` is available to drive anything else in the scene.

!!! tip
    Object flows travel with their object through sessions and undo: deleting an object and undoing brings its flow back intact.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md)

# Slider

An interactive slider that outputs a number — the quickest way to hand-tune any numeric input live.

**Output:** number

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| value | 20 | slider on the card |
| Min | 0 | ⓘ Params tab |
| Max | 40 | ⓘ Params tab |

The output is always clamped to the Min–Max range, so retune the range freely — stale values can't escape it.

## Practical example

1. Add a **Slider** and set **Min 0 / Max 5** in the ⓘ tab.
2. Add a **Spin** node and an **Object Selector** targeting your cube.
3. Wire Slider → Spin's **speed** input, and Spin → Object Selector.
4. Drag the slider: the cube's spin speed follows in real time — on every peer's screen.

!!! tip
    In older scenes a Slider wired *directly* into an Object Selector scales the target object (20 = neutral 1×). That legacy behavior still runs for saved graphs, but new graphs should drive a node parameter instead — it's clearer and works with any effect.

# Color Picker

Outputs a color chosen with a swatch — the color source for anything that paints.

**Output:** color

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| color | `#ff4000` | color swatch on the card |

## Practical example

1. Add a **Color Picker**, a **Set Color** node and an **Object Selector** targeting your cube.
2. Wire Color Picker → Set Color's **color** input, and Set Color → Object Selector.
3. Pick a color: the cube repaints instantly for everyone in the session.

!!! tip

In older scenes you may find a Color Picker wired straight into an Object Selector; that legacy connection still paints the object, but new graphs go through Set Color.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/switcher/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/switcher.md)

# Switcher

A radio-button list that outputs the **index** of the selected item — a hand-operated multi-way switch. Since 1.27
it is also a multi-way switch for **values**: each item has its own input, and the **value** output passes on whatever is
wired into the selected item.

**Outputs:**

| Output | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| (plain) | number | the selected item's index: 0, 1, 2… |
| value | the **Inputs carry** type | whatever is wired into the selected item's input |

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| index | number | chooses the item from the graph; a wired index overrides the radio buttons |
| one per item | the **Inputs carry** type | the value passed on while that item is selected |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| items | `cube`, `pyramid` | ⓘ Params tab — edit, add (**＋ Add item**) or remove entries |
| Inputs carry | number | ⓘ Params tab — number, boolean, vector3, color or object |
| selection | first item | radio buttons on the card |

## Switching values

Pick an item with its radio button, or wire a number into **index** to choose from the graph. The **value** output then
passes on the selected item's input — a speed, a colour, a target object.

- The plain output is still the selected index, so graphs made before 1.27 keep working unchanged.
- Removing an item in the ⓘ tab keeps the other wires on their items.
- Changing **Inputs carry** removes the wires the new type cannot accept, and a toast says how many.
  <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> brings them back.

## Practical example

Build a two-speed fan switch. Since 1.27 the shortest way is the **value** output: rename the items to `slow` and
`fast`, wire a **Number** of 0.5 into the `slow` input and one of 4 into `fast`, and wire **value** → a **Spin** node's
**speed** (Spin → an **Object Selector** targeting the fan, as below). The classic way, with the index and a [Select](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/select.md) node, still works:

1. Add a **Switcher** and rename its items to `slow`, `fast` (ⓘ tab).
2. Add a **Select** node; wire Switcher → Select's **index** input.
3. Add two **Number** nodes (0.5 and 4) wired into Select's **a** and **b**.
4. Wire Select → a **Spin** node's **speed** input, and Spin → an **Object Selector** targeting your fan object.
5. Click the radio buttons: the fan flips between slow and fast for everyone.

!!! tip
    The index output pairs naturally with [Select](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/select.md) (pick between two wired values) and [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md). Legacy note: in older scenes a Switcher with `cube`/`pyramid` items wired straight into an Object Selector swaps the target's geometry — kept working for saved graphs.

# Number

A constant numeric value — the simplest source node.

**Output:** number

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| value | 1 | number field on the card |
| Step | 1 | ⓘ Params tab — the increment the field's arrows use |

## Practical example

1. Add two **Number** nodes (say 3 and 4) and a **Math** node set to `mul`.
2. Wire them into Math's **a** and **b** inputs — the card shows the live result (12).
3. Wire Math → a **Bounce** node's **speed** input, and Bounce → an **Object Selector** targeting your cube: the cube bounces at the computed rate.

!!! tip
    Set **Step** to 0.1 (or smaller) when you're feeding parameters that live in a 0–1 range — the field's up/down arrows then move in useful increments.

# Vector3

An x/y/z triple — used as a direction, an offset, or most often a fixed **point in the world**.

**Output:** vector3

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| x, y, z | 0, 0, 0 | number fields on the card |

## Practical example

Make a signpost that always faces a spot:

1. Add a **Vector3** and set it to `0, 1, 5`.
2. Add a **Look At** node and an **Object Selector** targeting your sign.
3. Wire Vector3 → Look At's **target** input, and Look At → Object Selector.
4. Drag the sign around: it keeps turning to face the point at (0, 1, 5).

!!! tip
    A vector3 can stand in wherever an **object** is expected: wire one into [Distance](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/distance.md) or [Proximity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/proximity.md) to measure against a fixed world point instead of a second object.

# Toggle

A checkbox that outputs true or false — a hand-operated on/off switch.

**Output:** boolean

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| on | off (false) | checkbox on the card |

## Practical example

A light switch for a lamp object:

1. Add a **Toggle**, a **Visibility** node and an **Object Selector** targeting the lamp.
2. Wire Toggle → Visibility's **on** input, and Visibility → Object Selector.
3. Tick the checkbox: the lamp appears and disappears — for every peer at once.

!!! tip

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/random/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/random.md)

# Random

A random number in a range — deterministic, so every peer sees the *same* "random" value.

**Output:** number

## Inputs

`seed` (number) · `reroll` (event)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| min / max | 0 / 1 | fields on the card |
| interval | 0 | field on the card — seconds between re-rolls; 0 = one fixed value |
| integer | off | round down to a whole number, so the output can be used as an index |

Each Random node is seeded by its own identity and the shared clock: with `interval` set, it re-rolls every interval on all peers simultaneously; with `interval` 0 it holds one stable value.

### Seeding it yourself

Wire a number into `seed` and the value becomes a pure function of that number — same seed, same result, on every peer and every reload. That is what makes **procedural generation** authorable in a graph: one [Slider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md) or [Number](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/number.md) node is the seed for a whole layout, and typing 7 instead of 6 gives everybody the same different world.

Pulse `reroll` (from a [Key Press](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/keypress.md) or [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md)) to advance to the next value in the sequence without waiting for an interval.

## Seeded example

A "new layout" button that everyone agrees on:

1. **Number** (value 1) → **Random** `seed`, with min 0, max 4 and **integer** on.
2. **Key Press** (`KeyN`) → Random `reroll`.
3. Wire Random into a [Select](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/select.md) that picks one of several positions, then into an [Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md).
4. Press <kbd>N</kbd>: every peer jumps to the same next arrangement.

## Practical example

Give a hovering drone an erratic wobble:

1. Add a **Random** with min 0.5, max 3, interval 2.
2. Add a **Shake** node and an **Object Selector** targeting the drone.
3. Wire Random → Shake's **speed** input, and Shake → Object Selector.
4. Every 2 seconds the shake speed jumps to a new value — identical on every screen.

!!! tip
    Add several Random nodes for several independent streams — each node rolls its own sequence.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time.md)

# Time

The synced clock as a value — the heartbeat behind almost every animation recipe.

**Output:** number (live readout on the card)

## Inputs

None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| mode | sin | dropdown on the card: `t (seconds)`, `sin`, `saw`, `pingpong` |
| rate | 1 | slider on the card (0.1–5) — time multiplier |

Modes: **t** = raw seconds (ever-growing), **sin** = smooth wave −1…1, **saw** = ramp 0…1 that snaps back, **pingpong** = 0…1…0 triangle. All peers read the same shared clock, so the phase matches everywhere.

## Practical example

Make a cube's spin "breathe":

1. Add a **Time** node (mode `sin`).
2. Add a **Map Range** node: in −1…1 → out 0.2…2.
3. Wire Time → Map Range's **a**, Map Range → a **Spin** node's **speed** input, and Spin → an **Object Selector** targeting your cube.
4. The spin speed now swells and eases in a smooth loop.

!!! tip
    `sin` is centered on zero — pass it through [Map Range](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/maprange.md) whenever a parameter wants a positive range.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md)

# Object Selector

Binds the graph to a scene object — the **sink** every effect must reach, and an object *reference* for sensor nodes.

**Output:** object (a reference to the picked object — feeds [Distance](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/distance.md), [Proximity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/proximity.md), [Look At](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/lookat.md))

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| (left) | effect | any effect chain: animations, actions, Script, Sound, physics, module and custom nodes |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| object | `-None-` | dropdown of scene objects on the card |

## Practical example

1. Add a **Spin** node and an **Object Selector**.
2. Pick your cube in the Object Selector's dropdown.
3. Wire Spin → Object Selector: the cube starts spinning, in sync on every peer.
4. Add a second **Object Selector** picking the same cube and wire its *output* into a **Distance** node to measure from it — one node type, two roles.

!!! tip
    Effects only touch the scene **through** an Object Selector — a Spin node dangling on the canvas does nothing. If an object refuses to animate, check its right-click menu: *Disable flow effects* mutes a single object.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity.md)

# Velocity

Outputs how fast the connected object is moving right now, in metres per second.

**Output:** number

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| target | object | the object to measure — wire an [Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md), or leave it unwired inside an object's flow to measure that object |

Reads `0` when the object is at rest, and falls back to `0` if it stops receiving movement for about half a second.

## Local, not replicated

Each peer works out its own number. On the peer running the simulation it is exact; on the others it is an approximation from the ~10 movement updates a second that arrive over the network. Close enough to drive a speedometer or a colour ramp, but **don't** use it for anything that must match exactly on every screen — for that, drive the value from something deterministic (a [Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time.md) or [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md) node) instead.

## Practical example

A speedometer that glows:

1. Get something moving — throw a ball with the gizmo mid-simulation, or drive the car from the [modules](https://docs.theprototype.app/modules.md) library.
2. In its flow: **Velocity → Map Range** (in 0–12, out 0–1) → **Set Color**, so it shifts from blue to red as it speeds up.
3. Press <kbd>P</kbd>: the faster it moves, the hotter it looks.

!!! tip
    Feed Velocity into a [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md) node (`> 8`) plus a [Gate](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gate.md) to trigger something only above a speed threshold — a sparks burst when you're actually going fast.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/measure/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/measure.md)

# Measure

Reads a number off an object: how tall it is, where its top is, how fast it is going.

**Input:** `target` (object)
**Output:** number

## How it works

Measure reports one number at a time, picked by the `read` parameter. Sizes come from the object's **collider shape** — the same measurement the physics engine builds its body from — so what you read is what the simulation uses, and it costs nothing per frame.

Like [Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity.md), it is a local readout: every peer computes it from data everyone already has, so it puts nothing on the wire.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| read | top | `top` — the world Y of the object's highest point<br>`bottom` — the world Y of its lowest<br>`height` — how tall it is<br>`y` — the object's own position Y<br>`speed` — how fast it is moving (m/s) |

## Choosing the object

Wire an [Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md) into `target`, or drop the node unwired inside an object's own flow to read that object.

## Practical example

**"Is the stack tall enough?"**

1. **Object Selector** (the top crate) → **Measure** `target`, `read` = *top*.
2. **Measure → [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md)** `a`, with `b` = 3 and `op` = *greater than*.
3. The Compare output is a boolean you can wire into a [Gate](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gate.md), a [Visibility](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/visibility.md) node for a "win" sign, or a [HUD](https://docs.theprototype.app/node-system.md) readout.

**A speedometer.** `read` = *speed* → [Map Range](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/maprange.md) (0…20 → 0…1) → a [Set Color](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcolor.md) that reddens as the object goes faster.

**Where does it rest?** `read` = *bottom* tells you whether a crate is actually sitting on a pad or hovering above it.

!!! note
    `speed` is exact on the peer running the simulation and a close approximation elsewhere, because other peers derive it from the ~10 Hz position stream. Anything that must agree exactly between peers should be decided on the simulating peer.

## See also

- [Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity.md) — speed only, same local-readout rule
- [Distance](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/distance.md) — how far apart two objects are


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spawn/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spawn.md)

# Spawn

Makes copies of an object while the simulation runs — crates off a conveyor, targets, debris, ammo, waves of anything.

**Inputs:** `trigger` (event) · `at` (vector3 — an offset from the template) · `place` (vector3 — copies land exactly here; wins over `at`) · `source` (object — the template)
**Output:** effect (or wire the template into `source`)

## How it works

On the **rising edge** of whatever is wired into `trigger` — [Key Press](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/keypress.md), [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md), [Timer](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/timer.md), [On Enter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onenter.md) — the node copies its **template** object and drops the copy into the scene with a live physics body. The copy inherits the template's physics, material and geometry, so a dynamic template gives you something that falls.

Copies are **transient**. They live for the run and nothing else: they are never written into a saved scene, they leave nothing on the undo stack however many times you fire, and they all disappear when the simulation stops. That is the whole design — a run's debris is not scene content.

**A copy answers to its template's events.** Event nodes that target the template — an [On Hit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onhit.md), an [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md), an [On Enter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onenter.md) through an Object Selector — fire for its copies too, so a star you spawn behaves like the stars you placed.

**`place`** takes a point in the world: wire an [On Clap](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclap.md) `point` into it and the copy appears where the hands met.

The peer running the simulation makes the copy and everybody else receives it through the ordinary object sync, so two peers never disagree about what exists. Nothing extra goes on the wire for this node.

!!! warning "It needs a running simulation"
    A copy made with physics stopped would be inert, which is exactly the problem this node exists to remove — so with nothing simulating it refuses and says so instead of quietly doing nothing. Press <kbd>P</kbd> (or the ▶ button) **in the editor** first. You cannot start a simulation from inside Play mode; if you want both, turn on *simulate on play* in the scene's physics settings.

!!! tip "Give the template a body"
    If the template has no physics, the copies just hang in the air where they appear. Select it, then Inspector ▸ Physics ▸ Mode = *Dynamic*. The node warns you once when it notices.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| copies per fire | 1 | how many appear per event (hard limit 20) |
| max alive | 32 | how many this spawner keeps alive; when it is full, the **oldest** copy disappears as each new one arrives |
| min seconds between | 0 | a floor between fires. A trigger edge is not a rate limit on its own — a *held* key re-fires several times a second |
| spread | 0.5 | metres of random scatter, so a batch does not stack in one column |

There is also a **ceiling of 200 live copies across every spawner in the scene**, whatever the individual numbers say. An unbounded spawner in a shared session is both a memory problem and a griefing vector, so the limits are enforced when the copies are made and not merely suggested on the card.

## Where the copies appear

The `at` input (and the x/y/z on the card) is an **offset from the template**, not a world position — so a node with nothing wired drops copies just above an object you can already see. Wire a [Vector3](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/vector3.md) into `at` to aim it, or a [Math](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/math.md) chain if you want the point to move.

## Choosing the template

The same three ways as every other action node:

- **Object Selector → `source`** — "copy *that* object". The usual choice.
- **Nothing at all**, if the Spawn node lives in an object's own flow (double-click the object in the node editor's Graphs tree) — it copies that object.
- Keep the template somewhere visible in the scene. It stays editable, and a scene file that ships a spawner is self-documenting because you can see what it makes.

## Practical example

**A crate dispenser on a key.**

1. `/create box`, then Inspector ▸ Physics ▸ Mode = *Dynamic*. This is the template — move it somewhere visible and off the floor.
2. In the node editor add **Scene ▸ Spawn**.
3. Add **Triggers ▸ Key Press** (`code` = `KeyG`) → Spawn `trigger`.
4. Add an **Object Selector** naming the box → Spawn `source`.
5. Press <kbd>P</kbd> to start physics, then <kbd>G</kbd>: a copy appears 3 m above the template and falls.

**A burst.** Set *copies per fire* to 5 — five at once, scattered by *spread*.

**A capped fountain.** Set *max alive* to 8 and hold <kbd>G</kbd>: the count climbs to 8 and stays there, the oldest copy vanishing as each new one lands. That is the recycling, and it is what makes a spawner safe to leave running.

**A conveyor.** Drive `trigger` from a [Timer](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/timer.md) and set *min seconds between* to 2 for one crate every couple of seconds.

## Things worth knowing

- **Nothing spawns until the next real press** after you wire up a fresh Spawn node to a trigger that has already fired. That is deliberate: without it, a node arriving on a peer would adopt the last stamp it sees and spawn on connect.
- **Stopping the simulation removes every copy at once**, and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> will not bring them back — there is nothing to undo, by design.
- **Saving mid-run saves the template only.** Reload a scene you saved with forty crates in the air and you get the one box back.
- A copy does not carry the template's animation clips, object flow or shader graph. Each of those replicates a whole document per object, and volume is a spawner's whole point.

## See also

- [Impulse](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/impulse.md) — shove a copy the moment it appears
- [On Rest](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onrest.md) — fire when a spawned body has settled
- [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md) — count what you have made
- [Physics](https://docs.theprototype.app/physics.md) — bodies, ground, gravity and the simulation controls

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowinput/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowinput.md)

# Flow Input

Declares a **public input socket** for an [object flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows.md) — the way the Scene flow feeds a value into an object's own graph.

**Output:** the declared type (number / boolean / vector3 / color)

Only meaningful **inside an object flow**. In the Scene flow it has nothing to feed it and simply outputs its fallback.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| name | value | the socket label shown on the embedded [Object Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md) node |
| vtype | number | value type — number, boolean, vector3 or color |
| fallback | 0 | what the node outputs while nothing is wired into it from the Scene |

Changing the type resets the fallback to a sensible default for that type.

## How it behaves

Think of the object flow as a function and Flow Input as one of its parameters. Whatever the Scene wires into the matching socket of the embedded [Object Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md) node arrives here **on the same tick**. Unconnected, you get the fallback — so the object still behaves sensibly on its own.

Renaming or deleting the node updates the embedded card's sockets everywhere and disconnects any stale wire cleanly.

## Practical example

A lamp whose brightness the Scene controls:

1. Select a lamp object and create its flow.
2. Add **Flow Input** (name *brightness*, type number, fallback 1) and wire it into whatever drives the light.
3. In the Scene flow, right-click the lamp ▸ **Add flow to Scene graph**, then wire a [Slider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md) into the card's new *brightness* socket.
4. Drag the slider — the lamp reacts, and so does every peer's.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput.md)

# Flow Output

Declares a **public output socket** for an [object flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows.md) — the way an object publishes a value back to the Scene flow.

**Input:** any value type (the socket is gray = accepts anything)

Only meaningful **inside an object flow**.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| name | out | the socket label shown on the embedded [Object Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md) node |
| fallback | 0 | published while nothing is wired in |

## Values, not effects

Animation and effect nodes (Spin, Pulse, Sound… — the **orange** sockets) cannot wire into a Flow Output: they *do* something, they don't *carry* a value. Publish the value that drives them instead — the [Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time.md), [Math](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/math.md), [Slider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md) or [Loop](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/loop.md) node feeding the effect.

## One frame of latency

Outputs are collected at the end of a tick and delivered to the Scene on the **next** one. That single frame is invisible in practice and is what makes flows safe to compose without infinite loops.

## Practical example

A pressure plate that reports its state:

1. In the plate's flow, wire an [On Enter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onenter.md) → [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md) chain into a **Flow Output** named *presses*.
2. Embed the plate in the Scene flow (right-click ▸ **Add flow to Scene graph**).
3. In the Scene, wire the card's *presses* socket into a [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md) node (`>= 3`) and on into a door's [Object Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md) input — three presses, the door opens.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md)

# Object Flow

Embeds an object's own graph into the **Scene flow** as a single card — the way to compose [object flows](https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows.md) into a bigger machine without opening each one.

**Sockets:** whatever the embedded flow declares with [Flow Input](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowinput.md) / [Flow Output](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput.md)

## Adding one

- right-click the object in the viewport ▸ **Add flow to Scene graph** (an object with no flow gets one, with a Flow Input
  and a Flow Output to start from — one Undo; greyed out while someone else holds the object), or
- add an **Object Flow** node from the palette (*Object Flow* group) and pick the object.

Only objects that already **have** a flow are listed, and a flow can't embed itself.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| flowUuid | — | which object's flow this card represents (pick from the card) |

Double-click the card to open that object's flow in the editor.

## How it behaves

Values you wire **into** the card reach the flow's Flow Inputs on the same tick. Values the flow publishes through its Flow Outputs come out of the card on the **next** tick (one frame of latency — see [Flow Output](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput.md)).

The card's sockets track the flow's interface: rename, retype or delete a Flow Input/Output and every embedded card updates, dropping wires that no longer have a home. Delete the object's flow and its cards disappear with it.

## Practical example

One lamp design, three lamps:

1. Build the behaviour once in a lamp's flow, with a **Flow Input** *brightness* and a **Flow Output** *isOn*.
2. In the Scene flow, embed all three lamps as Object Flow cards.
3. Wire one [Slider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md) into all three *brightness* sockets — one control, three lamps, in sync for every peer.

!!! tip
    Prefer small object flows with a clear interface over one huge Scene graph: they travel with the object into [prefabs](https://docs.theprototype.app/prefabs.md) and saved scenes, and the Scene flow stays readable.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate.md)

# Set Game State

Switches the shared game state — `menu`, `playing`, `paused` or `over` — when a pulse arrives.
Every player follows the same state: it is the one switch a Start, Pause or Game Over button
writes to.

**Output:** none (an action)

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | event | each pulse makes the switch once — a [HUD Button](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudbutton.md), an [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md), a [Delay](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/delay.md), [All Players](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/allplayers.md) |

The trigger needs a **pulse**. A true/false value (a [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md)) wired straight in
does nothing; put an event node such as [All Players](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/allplayers.md) between them.

!!! warning "Known problem in 1.42"
    The card does not draw its **trigger** socket yet, so this node cannot be wired by hand in the node editor. Until
    that is fixed, let the HUD editor build it: select a button and pick one of the game actions (see the tip at the end
    of this page) — the action adds a Set Game State already wired to the button.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| state | playing | `menu`, `playing`, `paused`, `over` |
| outcome | (empty) | a short word stored with the state, up to 40 characters — `won`, `lost` — meant for `over` |
| full reset | off | on: back to `menu` **and** the round clock to zero, whatever `state` says |

## What each state does

- **playing** from `menu` or `over` starts a **new round**: the round number goes up by one and
  the round clock ([Game Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gametime.md)) starts again from 0. From `paused` it **resumes**
  the same round, and the clock carries on where it stopped.
- **paused** stops physics, animations and the round clock for everybody. Flow logic and the HUD
  keep running, so a pause menu still works.
- **over** ends the round with the `outcome` text. The clock is not zeroed.
- **menu** goes back to the menu. Only **full reset** also zeroes the round clock, so a Game Time
  readout on the menu shows 0 instead of the last round's time. A reset keeps the round count and
  the variables.

HUD screens set to show **while** a state (see [HUD Editor](https://docs.theprototype.app/hud-editor.md)) and
[Game Start](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamestart.md) nodes react to the state by themselves; [On Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate.md)
pulses when it changes.

## In multiplayer

The pulse is shared, so every player's copy of the graph makes the same switch at the same
moment, and the newest write wins. It does not matter who pressed the button. A player who joins
later receives the current state, round, clock and outcome on arrival. A Set Game State node you
add only acts on pulses that come **after** it was placed: an old click never starts a game.

The state is saved with the scene. Leaving Play on your own puts the game back on its menu; with
other people in the session, the game resets once the last player has been out of Play for ten
seconds.

## Practical example

A start button and a pause key:

1. Add an **On Click** and an **Object Selector** picking a `Start` box; wire On Click → Object Selector.
2. Add a **Set Game State** (state `playing`); wire On Click → its **trigger**.
3. Add a **Key Press** (capture <kbd>P</kbd>) and a second **Set Game State** (state `paused`);
   wire Key Press → its **trigger**.
4. Press Play and click the box: the round starts for everyone. <kbd>P</kbd> pauses it, and a
   click on the box resumes it.

![The example's nodes: On Click on the Start box, a Key Press for P, and two Set Game State cards (playing, paused) — in 1.42 the cards have no trigger socket to wire into](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-setgamestate/setgamestate.webp)
*Figure: The example's nodes.*
!!! tip
    The HUD editor builds these for you: select a button and pick **Actions ▸ Start the game**,
    **Pause**, **Resume**, **End the game**, **Back to the menu** or **Reset the game**.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate.md)

# On Game State

Fires a pulse when the shared game state becomes the one you pick — the hook for "when the round
starts" or "when the game is over". With **edge** `exit` it fires when the game *leaves* that
state instead.

**Output:** event — 1 for a short moment (0.3 s) after the change, otherwise 0

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| state | playing | `menu`, `playing`, `paused`, `over` |
| edge | enter | `enter` (the game switched **to** this state), `exit` (it switched **away** from it) |

## How it fires

The game state itself is shared (see [Set Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate.md)). Each player's copy of the
graph watches it and pulses this node on its own when the state changes. The pulse itself is
never sent over the network, so each player gets exactly one pulse per change.

- **Resuming counts as entering `playing`.** `paused` → `playing` fires `playing` / `enter` just
  like a fresh start does. If something must happen only at the start of a new round, drive it
  from the Start button's own pulse instead.
- **It is not a replay.** A player who joins mid-round receives the current state, not the
  pulses they missed. Anything that has to be right for a late arrival — which screen shows,
  which camera you look through — is better bound to the state itself: a HUD screen's **while**
  setting ([HUD Editor](https://docs.theprototype.app/hud-editor.md)), a [Game Start](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamestart.md) node, or
  [Game Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gametime.md) `playing`.

## Practical example

Keep each player's best score when a game ends:

1. Add an **On Game State** with state `over`, edge `enter`.
2. Add a **Store Value** (key `mygame-best`, mode `max`); wire On Game State → its **trigger**.
3. Add a **Get Variable** (name `score`); wire it → Store Value's **value**.
4. Every time the game reaches `over`, each player's device keeps the higher of its saved best
   and the final score.

![On Game State (over) pulses a Store Value whose value comes from Get Variable score](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-ongamestate/ongamestate.webp)
*Figure: On Game State (over) pulses a Store Value whose value comes from Get Variable score.*
!!! tip
    Wired into a number input, On Game State reads 1 for the moment after the change and 0
    otherwise, just like [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md).


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera.md)

# Set Active Camera

Makes a camera object the active view for every player when a pulse arrives.

**Output:** effect (through an Object Selector, or its own camera input)

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | event | the pulse that switches the view |
| camera | object | the camera object to make active (or the node's `camera` parameter) |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| camera | (none) | a camera object's uuid, picked on the card |

## Practical example

Wire an **On Enter** trigger volume at a doorway into **Set Active Camera** with the room's camera: walking through the door cuts to that room's view for every player.

# Camera Rig

Moves a scene [camera object](https://docs.theprototype.app/camera.md#camera-objects) so it follows a target, looks at it, or both — a chase
camera behind a car, a camera that keeps a player in frame. New in 1.27; find it in the palette under **Game**.

**Output:** effect (wire into an [Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md) that picks a camera)

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| target | object | what to follow and look at — an [Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md) |
| offset | vector3 | the offset from the target; wire a [Vector3](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/vector3.md) here instead of using **ox / oy / oz** |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| mode | both | **both**, **follow** (position only) or **lookat** (turn only) |
| space | world | **world**, or **target**: the offset turns with the target — use it for a chase camera that stays behind a car |
| ox / oy / oz | 0 / 2 / 5 | the offset from the target, in metres |
| damping | 0.25 | seconds of lag; 0 follows rigidly |
| aim | 0 | a height above the target to look at |

## Practical example

A chase camera for a car:

1. Add a camera: right-click ▸ **Add ▸ Camera ▸ Perspective**.
2. Add a **Camera Rig** and wire it into an **Object Selector** that picks the camera. (Or put the Camera Rig in the
   camera's own graph, where it moves that camera with no Object Selector.)
3. Wire a second **Object Selector**, picking the car, into **target**.
4. Set **space** to *target*. The offset is now measured along the car's own axes: the defaults (**oy** 2, **oz** 5)
   put the camera 2 m up and 5 m along the car's Z axis — if it ends up in front of the car, make **oz** −5. The camera
   now stays behind the car and turns with it.
5. To see through the camera, use [Set Active Camera](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera.md) or the camera's **Preview**.

![A camera object, its viewing pyramid drawn, aimed at a cube by a Camera Rig](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-camerarig/camera-rig.webp)
*Figure: A camera object.*
## Limits

- It moves camera objects only. Wired to anything else it does nothing, and a toast says so.
- It never moves the editor view or another player's view. Every player's copy of the camera follows on their own
  screen.
- While a rig is attached, the rig decides where the camera is. Remove the rig and the camera goes back to where you
  placed it.

!!! tip
    The older **Camera Follow** node (under **Character**) moves the *player's* view behind an object. Camera Rig moves a
    camera object instead, so a game can cut between several rigged cameras with Set Active Camera.


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setlook/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setlook.md)

# Set Look

Switches a camera's **look** — its [post-processing](https://docs.theprototype.app/post-processing.md) — on or off when a pulse arrives, and by
default also looks through that camera.

**Output:** effect

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | event | when to apply it |
| camera | object | the camera whose look to switch. Unwired = the scene's own look |
| on | boolean | true turns the look on, false turns it off |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| on | true | the value used when `on` is not wired |
| activate | true | **look through it too** — also make that camera the active view, because a camera's look only shows while you look through it |

Each player applies it on their own screen when the (shared) trigger arrives, so every view ends up the same without a
message of its own. It changes what you see, never the scene's saved look.

If you switch **activate** off and nobody is looking through that camera, nothing changes on screen — the app says so
once, and suggests a [Set Active Camera](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera.md) node.

## Practical example

A dream sequence: a **Game Start** pulse into **Set Look** with the *Dream cam* wired into `camera` — every player cuts
to that camera with its soft-focus look. A second Set Look with **on** false on the round's end turns it off again.
See [Switching looks from a node graph](https://docs.theprototype.app/post-processing.md#switching-looks-from-a-node-graph).

# All Players

Fires a pulse once **every player in Play** answers yes to a condition — the group gate that
makes sure nobody is left behind ("everyone is at the portal", "everyone has three laps").

**Output:** event — wire it into a [Travel to scene](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/travel.md) node's trigger,
a [Set Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate.md), or anything else a pulse drives

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| condition | boolean | each player answers for themselves — a [Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md), a [Latch](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/latch.md), anything true/false |

Unwired, the answer is no, and the node never fires.

## Who counts

- Each player's copy of the graph works out the condition **for that player** and shares only
  the yes/no answer. When every player in Play says yes, every copy fires the node on its own
  (nothing extra is sent, so the pulse is not doubled).
- **Only players in Play count.** Someone sitting in the editor is a spectator: they never hold
  the group up. If nobody is in Play, nobody is ready and the node does not fire.
- It fires on the change from "not everyone" to "everyone". If one player drops back to no and
  then says yes again, it fires again.

The answer is only as personal as the condition you wire in. A per-player value such as
[Player Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/peervariable.md) `mine` gives a real per-player answer; a shared value (a
[Get Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md), a [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md)) is the same for everyone, so the gate then
simply fires when that shared condition comes true while somebody is playing.

## Practical example

End the race when every player has done three laps:

1. Add a **Player Variable** (name `laps`, read `mine`).
2. Add a **Compare** (op `gte`, b = 3); wire Player Variable → its **a**.
3. Add an **All Players**; wire Compare → its **condition**.
4. Add a **Set Game State** (state `over`, outcome `finished`); wire All Players → its **trigger**.

Each player's own `laps` comes from a [Set Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable.md) with scope `player`.

![A Player Variable (laps, mine) into a Compare (≥ 3), into All Players' condition, into Set Game State (over)](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-allplayers/allplayers.webp)
*Figure: A Player Variable (laps.*
!!! tip
    All Players also works as a "this just came true" detector for a shared condition: a
    Compare cannot drive a trigger input directly, but Compare → All Players → Set Game State
    can (as long as someone is in Play).


---

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable.md)

# Set Variable

Writes a named number when a pulse arrives — a score, lives, a difficulty. With scope `shared` it
is one number the whole game shares, with no object needed to hold it; with scope `player` it is
**your own** number, one per player.

**Output:** none (an action)

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | event | each pulse writes once — an [On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md), a [HUD Button](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudbutton.md), an [On Hit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onhit.md), [On Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate.md) |
| value | number | the amount to set, add or subtract — wire a [Number](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/number.md), a [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md), a [Math](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/math.md) result (unwired: 0) |

The card has no field for the value: wire one in. The HUD editor's **Actions ▸ Set a variable**
builds a Set Variable that adds 1 to `score`.

!!! warning "Known problem in 1.42"
    The card does not draw its **trigger** and **value** sockets yet, so this node cannot be wired by hand in the node
    editor. Until that is fixed, let the HUD editor build it: select a button and pick **Actions ▸ Set a variable**,
    which adds a Set Variable already wired to the button (it adds 1 to `score`).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| name | `score` | the variable's name, up to 40 characters |
| op | set | `set` (replace), `add`, `subtract` |
| scope | shared | `shared` (one number for the game), `player` (this player's own row) |

## Shared or per player

| | `shared` | `player` |
|---|---|---|
| Read it with | [Get Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md) | [Player Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/peervariable.md), [Leaderboard](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/leaderboard.md) |
| Who writes it | every player's copy of the graph, newest write wins | only the player it belongs to |
| A player who joins later | gets it with the game state | gets every player's row when they connect |
| Kept | with the scene when it is saved, and across [Travel to scene](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/travel.md) | while the player is connected, across Travel too; leaving Play keeps it, and when they disconnect the others drop it. Not saved with the scene |

Neither kind is reset by a new round. A game that wants a fresh start writes it: a Set Variable with
op `set` and nothing wired into **value** (0), driven by the Start button's pulse.

**The trigger decides who acts, the scope decides whose number.** A shared pulse (an ordinary
On Click) runs the node on every player's copy of the graph. Into a `player`-scope Set Variable,
that adds to **everybody's** own number ("everyone scores when the boss falls"). A pulse only one
player sees — an [On Hit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onhit.md) with who `me` — adds to that player's number alone.

!!! note "One event, one change (since 1.48.1)"
    A shared pulse runs the node on every player's copy, but a `shared` variable changes **once**
    for the whole session: one click adds 1 once, and a toggle (`set` to NOT the value) flips once.
    Before 1.48.1 every player applied the change itself, so `add` could count two or three times.
    A `player`-scope variable has only one writer, so it never doubled up.

A player can hold up to 64 per-player names. Variables are separate from
[Store Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md), which keeps a number on one device across reloads and never shares
it.

## Practical example

Add a point to the shared score with each click on a coin:

1. Add an **On Click** and an **Object Selector** picking the `Coin`; wire On Click → Object Selector.
2. Add a **Set Variable** (name `score`, op `add`, scope `shared`); wire On Click → its **trigger**.
3. Add a **Number** (value 1); wire it → Set Variable's **value**.
4. Read the score with a [Get Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md) named `score`, or show it on screen with
   the HUD editor's **Actions ▸ Show a variable**.

![The example's nodes: On Click on the Coin, a Set Variable (score, add, shared) and a Number set to 1 — in 1.42 the Set Variable card has no sockets to wire into](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-setvariable/setvariable.webp)
*Figure: The example's nodes.*

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md)

# Get Variable

Reads a named shared variable as a number — the read side of [Set Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable.md),
live on every player's screen.

**Output:** number (shown live on the card)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| name | `score` | the variable to read — the same name the Set Variable writes |

A name nothing has written yet reads as 0.

## What it reads

Get Variable reads the **shared** variables: the ones a Set Variable with scope `shared` writes,
and the shared count of the Collectibles module. They travel with the game state, so every
player — including one who joins later — reads the same number, and the read itself sends
nothing.

It does not read per-player numbers (Set Variable scope `player`); use
[Player Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/peervariable.md) for those. It does not read what [Store Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md)
saved on the device either; that is [Stored Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue.md).

## Practical example

A door that disappears once the team has 10 points:

1. Add a **Get Variable** (name `score`).
2. Add a **Compare** (op `lt`, b = 10); wire Get Variable → its **a**.
3. Add a **Visibility** node; wire Compare → its **on**.
4. Add an **Object Selector** picking the `Door`; wire Visibility → Object Selector. The door
   stays while the score is under 10 and vanishes for everyone when it reaches 10.

![Get Variable score into a Compare (less than 10), driving a Visibility node on the Door's Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/img/nodes-getvariable/getvariable.webp)
*Figure: Get Variable score into a Compare (less than 10).*
!!! tip
    To show a variable on screen, select a HUD Text element and pick **Actions ▸ Show a
    variable** in the HUD editor: it wires a Get Variable into a [HUD Text](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudtext.md) for you.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md)

# Store Value

Saves a value **on this device** when a pulse arrives — a best score, the tallest tower, the
level a player reached — so it survives a reload. It is never sent to other players and never
written into the scene file.

**Output:** none (a sink)

## Inputs

| Handle | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | event | each pulse writes once — wire [On Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes.md#game) (`over`), a [HUD Button](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudbutton.md) or a Counter |
| value | number | what to save — wire a [Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md), a Get Variable, a Measure |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| key | `best` | the name it is saved under — give each game its own (`towers-best`, not `best`) |
| mode | max | `set` (overwrite), `max` (keep the highest), `min` (keep the lowest — a best time), `add` (a running total) |

## How it is stored

Values live in the browser's local storage under `tp:scene:<scene name>:<key>`. A game loaded
from the Games tab has no scene name yet, so it uses `untitled` — which is why every game should
use a **game-specific key**, or two games' bests would share one slot.

Each player keeps their own copy. A trigger that fires for everyone (a shared Game State) saves
on every device; a per-player trigger saves only for the player who earned it.

## Practical example

"Best height" in Towers:

1. **On Game State** (`over`) → Store Value's **trigger**.
2. The round's tallest height (a Math `max` over the ring latches) → **value**.
3. key `towers-best`, mode `max`.
4. A [Stored Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue.md) with the same key feeds the Round-over screen's HUD Text.

!!! tip
    A round-scoped latch reads "not set" the instant the round ends, so a Round-over screen
    should read the STORED value, not the latch. Write a `set 0` at round start and a `max` on
    every hit.

The HUD editor's **Actions → Save best score** builds this chain for a button in one step.

Source: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue/ (Markdown: https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue.md)

# Stored Value

Reads what a [Store Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md) node saved **on this device** — the read side of a best
score. Each player sees their own number.

**Output:** number or text (shown live on the card)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|
| key | `best` | the same key the Store Value writes |
| output | number | `number`, or `text` for a saved string |

Nothing saved yet reads as the fallback (0).

## Practical example

Show "Best: 12 m" on a menu screen: Stored Value (key `towers-best`) → a **HUD Text** with the
format `Best: {v} m`. The number updates the moment a Store Value writes it.

Modules can read and write the same kind of storage through `api.storage` — see
[Module SDK](https://docs.theprototype.app/module-sdk.md).
